::: {.lead}
Two sharp measurements can be performed jointly only if they **commute**. So run them **in both orders at once**, and let interference reveal whether the order mattered.
:::

<!-- ===================================================================== -->
::::: {.layer num="01" label="Question" title="Can two measurements be performed jointly?"}

:::: {.poster-grid widths="1fr, 1.35fr"}

::: {.col}
::: {.panel title="Compatibility"}
Observables $A$, $B$ with spectral projectors $\{P_i\}$, $\{Q_j\}$ are **compatible** if one measurement reproduces the statistics of both. For sharp observables this holds iff $[P_i,Q_j]=0$ for all $i,j$.

::: {.placeholder height="7.5cm"}
Fig. 1 — Compatible ($\sigma_z,\sigma_z$) vs. incompatible ($\sigma_z,\sigma_x$) eigenbases on the Bloch sphere.
:::
:::
:::

::: {.col}
::: {.panel title="Two ways to decide"}
*Standard route.* Cost grows with the dimension $d$.

:::: {.flow}
::: {.col}
Process tomography of both measurements
:::
::: {.col}
Semidefinite feasibility test
:::
::: {.col}
Compatible: yes / no
:::
::::

*Switch route.* Sample complexity **independent of $d$**.

:::: {.flow}
::: {.col}
Apply $\mathcal{A}$, $\mathcal{B}$ in superposed orders
:::
::: {.col}
Measure the control qubit
:::
::: {.col .hl}
One number, $p_-$
:::
::::
:::
:::

::::

:::::

::: {.bridge}
If the order of $\mathcal{A}$ and $\mathcal{B}$ matters, put both orders in superposition and let them interfere.
:::

<!-- ===================================================================== -->
::::: {.layer num="02" label="Principle" title="The quantum SWITCH turns non-commutativity into interference"}

:::: {.poster-grid widths="1fr, 1.35fr"}

::: {.col}
::: {.panel title="Circuit"}
::: {.placeholder height="11cm"}
Fig. 2 — Quantum SWITCH: control $\lvert +\rangle$ chooses [$\mathcal{A}$ then $\mathcal{B}$]{.ab} or [$\mathcal{B}$ then $\mathcal{A}$]{.ba}; the control is then measured in the Fourier basis.
:::
:::
:::

::: {.col}
::: {.panel title="From a click rate to an incompatibility measure"}
:::: {.flow}
::: {.col}
$p_-$\
"$-$" on the control
:::
::: {.col}
$\mathrm{NCOM}_\rho=\sqrt{2p_-}$\
non-commutativity
:::
::: {.col .hl}
$\mathrm{MED}_\rho$\
incompatibility
:::
::::

$$
p_- = \tfrac{1}{4}\sum_{i,j}\operatorname{Tr}\left(\rho\,\lvert[C_i,D_j]\rvert^2\right),
\qquad
\mathrm{MED}_\rho = \sqrt{1-\operatorname{Re}\sum_{i,j}\operatorname{Tr}\left[\rho\,P_iQ_jP_iQ_j\right]}
$$

::: {.keybox}
**For sharp observables $\mathrm{NCOM}_\rho = \mathrm{MED}_\rho$ exactly:** one interference fringe certifies incompatibility. No tomography, no SDP [1].
:::
:::
:::

::::

:::::

::: {.bridge}
Build it with a single photon: polarization is the system, arrival time is the switch.
:::

<!-- ===================================================================== -->
::::: {.layer num="03" label="Realisation" title="A time-bin switch that is stable by construction"}

:::: {.poster-grid widths="1fr, 1.15fr, 1fr"}

::: {.col}
::: {.panel title="Dictionary"}
| Concept | Photonic element |
|:--------|:-----------------|
| System $\rho$ | polarization qubit |
| Control qubit | time bins $\lvert e\rangle,\lvert l\rangle$ |
| [Order $\mathcal{A}\mathcal{B}$]{.ab} / [order $\mathcal{B}\mathcal{A}$]{.ba} | [early]{.ab} / [late]{.ba} bin |
| Lüders channel $\mathcal{A}$ | QWP + HWP + calcite |
| Environment | temporal wavepacket |
:::
:::

::: {.col}
::: {.panel title="Setup"}
::: {.placeholder height="14cm"}
Fig. 3 — Heralded polarization qubit, time-bin control, waveplates + calcite for each block, interference of the control.
:::
:::
:::

::: {.col}
::: {.panel title="Dephasing by walk-off"}
Calcite delays $\lvert V\rangle$ by $\Delta\tau = L\,\Delta n_g/c$; tracing out time leaves $\mathcal{A}(\rho)=\sum_i P_i\rho P_i$ once $\Delta\tau\gg\tau_{\text{coh}}$.

::: {.note}
$\tau_{\text{coh}} = 3.3\,\text{ps} \ll \Delta\tau_{A,B} \approx 10\text{–}18\,\text{ps} \ll \Delta t_c = 150\,\text{ns}$
:::
:::

::: {.panel title="Why it is stable"}
Delays commute, $T_{\tau_A}T_{\tau_B}=T_{\tau_B}T_{\tau_A}$: both orders leave **identical wavepackets**. No active stabilization needed.
:::
:::

::::

:::::

::: {.bridge}
Test it on qubits, then ask what the signal means beyond projective measurements.
:::

::: {.col}
::: {.panel title="Beyond sharp measurements"}
For **POVMs**, commutativity is no longer necessary for joint measurability; what the switch certifies there must be established anew.
:::
